item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Putin’s 2024 record on `3B.5` is mostly negative. I found only weak evidence of narrow, rule-bound internal discipline; the dominant pattern is surveillance, censorship, and administrative control used to monitor foreigners and constrain dissent.

**Accepted Claims**

**Weak evidence for narrow/lawful use**

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Decree amending military statutes](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print) | President of Russia | 2024-03-01 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Putin required commanders to prevent crimes and incidents, immediately report weapon loss, notify the military prosecutor / investigators / FSB, and personally take part in investigations of serious catastrophes and violent crimes inside units. This is real procedural discipline, but it is internal military governance rather than independent civilian oversight. | `3B.5`, weakly `3B.1` |
| [Biometric system in Moscow](https://government.ru/docs/all/155077/) | Government of Russia | 2024-08-26 | https://government.ru/docs/all/155077/ | The Moscow biometric decree included a refusal clause: if a person had filed an objection, their biometrics could not be collected until they revoked it. That is a formal safeguard, but it sits inside a broader biometric surveillance architecture. | `3B.5` |

**Strong evidence against narrow/lawful use**

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Law on communications services to foreign nationals and social-media disclosures](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/74828) | President of Russia | 2024-08-08 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/74828 | Putin signed a law requiring foreigners to verify identity through the biometric system for mobile contracts, limiting SIM cards, and forcing social-media platforms to hand user information to Roskomnadzor or the FSB and label large accounts. This is expansive surveillance and control, not narrowly tailored security use. | `3B.5`, also `3B.2`, `3B.3` |
| [Biometric border experiment for foreign nationals](https://mintrans.gov.ru/eye/press-center/news/11605) | Ministry of Transport of Russia | 2024-11-27 | https://mintrans.gov.ru/eye/press-center/news/11605 | From December 1, 2024, foreigners entering or leaving Russia through major airports and one land checkpoint had to submit biometrics; the second phase extended the system more broadly to visa-free visitors. The measure is framed as migration control, but it is still broad administrative surveillance of outsiders. | `3B.5`, also `3B.2` |
| [Law expanding extremist/terrorist designations](https://tass.ru/obschestvo/22793553) | TASS | 2024-12-28 | https://tass.ru/obschestvo/22793553 | Putin signed a law expanding the grounds for listing people as extremists or terrorists and giving Rosfinmonitoring access to the bank information of people financially supporting extremism. That is a punitive control tool with obvious abuse potential, especially against political opponents. | `3B.5`, also `3B.2`, `3B.3` |
| [Russia: Freedom on the Net 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-net/2024 | Freedom House reports that in March 2024 Russia banned information about bypassing blocks and VPN advertising, and that Roskomnadzor’s blocking powers were being expanded. This shows censorship and administrative control used to restrict access and deter circumvention, not lawful restraint. | `3B.5`, also `3B.3` |

**Search Gap**
I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Putin created genuinely independent complaint-handling, civilian oversight, or abuse-investigation mechanisms with meaningful autonomy or public accountability. The closest “for” material was procedural discipline inside the military and a limited biometric refusal clause, both of which fall far short of independent oversight.
